entries.whatsWrong: The attendee could not tell which Lean Six Sigma training was the appropriate option among DES, Transformational Healthcare Team, and OSI, so they contacted each program.
entries.whoFeels: The attendee, particularly staff trying to identify the appropriate program.
entries.evidence: "Which has a fee. So I was confused about that."; "not being sure which one I was supposed to apply for"; "I emailed each of them and kind of asked."

entries.whatsWrong: UC Learning displayed an error during registration, and the attendee could register only after identifying and checking an acknowledgement checkbox.
entries.whoFeels: The attendee registering through UC Learning; OSI also receives the resulting registration question.
entries.evidence: "I went into that platform and used my AD login and tried to register for the class, but I got, like, an error"; "I had to email the OSI inbox and ask them maybe what the error was about"; "some acknowledgement, like a checkbox that was in the UC Learning platform"

entries.whatsWrong: Adding virtual attendees to the Teams environment requires Tony to add each person individually because there is no batch-add capability.
entries.whoFeels: Tony and the Yellow Belt delivery team managing virtual-session access.
entries.evidence: "I add, one by one, every single person that's, um, going to be attending the virtual, uh, into the Teams environment. I have to add them manually, because there's not a batch way to add them"

entries.where: Receive the certificate and consider next steps
entries.whatsWrong: After completing the training, the attendee experienced information overload and was unsure how to proceed or practice what they had learned.
entries.whoFeels: The attendee after receiving the certificate and completing the Zoom sessions.
entries.evidence: "I feel a little bit overwhelmed. A little unsure of where to go next. Because it was a lot of information kind of overload"; "I'm looking for ways to practice what I learned"
